Department Marketing Statement

Student Health is a full service on campus primary healthcare facility for UCSB students. We see students on both an appointment and walk in basis. Our auxiliary services included on-site laboratory, pharmacy, and x-ray. Our specialty services include psychiatry and sports medicine.

Benefits Of Belonging

Working at UC means being part of this vibrant institution that shines a light on what is possible. People make UC great, and UC recognizes your contributions by making this a great place to work. Excellent retirement and health are just one of the rewards. Learn more about the benefits of working at UC

Brief Summary Of Job Duties

The Transitional Executive Director for Student Health / Assistant Vice Chancellor for Integrated Care (AVC/ED) provides overall strategic and operational leadership for Student Health Services (SHS), driving high-quality, cost-effective care that supports the academic mission and wellbeing of over 25,000 students. The AVC/ED manages daily operations through subordinate managers and senior directors across diverse clinical and administrative disciplines, including primary care, behavioral health, psychiatry, ancillary services, and the Student Health Insurance Plan (SHIP). The position holds primary accountability for a $30+ million budget, ~100 FTE staff, regulatory compliance, risk management, and the overall financial, operational, and physical infrastructure of the health system.

Reporting to the Associate Vice Chancellor for Student Wellbeing, this two-year executive appointment provides strategic leadership for implementing organizational improvements identified through a 2026 external review of UC Santa Barbara's Student Health Service and Behavioral Health System of Care planning process. The position leads the development of Student Health's strategic plan, and advances an integrated behavioral health model across Student Health Service, Counseling & Psychological Services, and campus partners, and directs complex organizational change initiatives. Through executive oversight of senior leadership, strategic planning, organizational development, and financial sustainability initiatives, the incumbent is accountable for implementing a coordinated behavioral health system that improves access, care navigation, operational effectiveness, performance outcomes, and long-term organizational sustainability.

Required Qualifications

Master’s degree in Public Health, Healthcare Administration or related fields along with at least 10 years of relevant experience in a leadership or administrative role OR
M.D., Ph.D., Psy.D. or other clinical training along with at least five years of relevant experience in healthcare administration in a leadership role.

Preferred Qualifications

Executive Leadership role in College health care setting.
Experience with physical and psychological health care integration.

Special Conditions Of Employment

This is a two year contract position.
Mandated reporting requirements of Child Abuse
UCSB Campus Security Authority under Clery Act
Works in patient care environment
Satisfactory criminal history background check
UCSB is a Tobacco-Free environment

Misconduct Disclosure Requirement

As a condition of employment, the final candidate who accepts an offer of employment will be required to disclose if they have been subject to any final administrative or judicial decisions within the last seven years determining that they committed any misconduct; or have filed an appeal of a finding of substantiated misconduct with a previous employer.

“Misconduct” Means Any Violation Of The Policies Governing Employee Conduct At The Applicant’s Previous Place Of Employment, Including, But Not Limited To, Violations Of Policies Prohibiting Sexual Harassment, Sexual Assault, Or Other Forms Of Harassment, Or Discrimination, As Defined By The Employer. For Reference, Below Are UC’s Policies Addressing Some Forms Of Misconduct

UC Sexual Violence and Sexual Harassment Policy

UC Anti-Discrimination Policy

Abusive Conduct in the Workplace\

Job Functions And Percentages Of Time

30% Change Management and Organizational Transformation

Strategic Planning & Executive Governance: Directs the Student Health Service executive team in formulating multi-year strategic plans and long-term policies, establishing organizational vision and operational goals that align service delivery with campus needs, care access, and fiscal sustainability.

Operational Transformation & Process Improvement: Exercises high-level administrative authority to execute operational recommendations from the 2026 external review, establishing systems and operational controls to optimize:

Workforce Configuration: Aligning staffing models and FTE allocation with patient demand.
Provider Productivity: Formulating and monitoring daily provider encounter benchmarks.
Billing Expansion & Revenue Optimization: Directing revenue cycle infrastructure and billing team growth.
Coding Education: Overseeing clinical documentation standards and provider feedback loops.

In consultation with the AVC for Student Wellbeing, directs the ongoing rollout of broad report initiatives.

Integrated Care Model Leadership: Provides executive oversight and program evaluation for the large-scale integration and transformation of behavioral health services spanning Student Health Service, Counseling & Psychological Services (CAPS), and campus-wide wellbeing programs. Establishes executive priorities, institutional policy, and implementation frameworks across the Wellbeing Cluster to advance an operationalized, student-centered behavioral health system of care.

Change Management & Organizational Alignment: Directs executive change management strategies and organizational design frameworks to foster interdisciplinary collaboration, inter-departmental alignment, and broad adoption of modernized operating models.

Senior Leadership Advisory: Advises Wellbeing Cluster leadership and campus executives on complex, high-stakes organizational change initiatives, ensuring strict compliance with regulatory mandates, risk management standards, and strategic campus priorities.

Resource & Infrastructure Stewardship: Directs the operational, human resource, and financial infrastructure across the cluster, aligning multi-million-dollar budgets and staffing strategies to sustain the integrated health model.

Special Executive Projects: Performs other high-level healthcare administration and policy duties as assigned by the Associate Vice Chancellor for Student Wellbeing.

50% Operational & Strategic Leadership

Strategic Adaptation & Program Evaluation: Analyzes, evaluates, and adapts Student Health Service through subordinate leadership to respond to evolving student healthcare needs, public health challenges, accreditation and licensing requirements, and funding landscapes.

Strategic Planning & Policy Execution: Formulates and executes strategic action plans, establishing the vision, long-term goals, and operational policies needed to address emerging campus health priorities.

Financial Oversight & Resource Optimization: Monitors and directs financial management, healthcare utilization, cost-containment strategies, and overall organizational design for a large, complex health department to ensure long-term fiscal sustainability.

Comprehensive Care Delivery: Holds executive accountability for the delivery of high-quality, accessible primary, behavioral, and ancillary healthcare services to students by organizing and leveraging integrated on- and off-campus health resources. UC SHIP Governance: Exercises executive responsibility for the oversight, financial design, and utilization of the UC Student Health Insurance Plan (UC SHIP), collaborating with local leadership and actively representing the campus on UC Systemwide Advisory Boards and Implementation Teams.

UC Systemwide Alignment & Collaboration: Collaborates with peer UC Student Health Directors to coordinate cross-campus care models, monitor systemwide costs, arrange care reciprocity, and influence university-wide health policies.

Public Relations & Institutional Integrity: Maintains institutional integrity, protects organizational reputation, and leads public health messaging by serving as the approved authority for campus communications, media requests, and community relations.

20% Resource Management

Fiscal Leadership & Budgetary Control: Accountable for managing a $30+ million budget derived from complex, multi-source funding models; leads the preparation, advocacy, and strategic management of short- and long-term financial plans to ensure long-term organizational viability.

Revenue Optimization & Strategic Analysis: Directs the strategic analysis and development of revenue-generating initiatives across Student Health Service and Counseling & Psychological Services, including third-party billing models, behavioral health reimbursement expansion, and clinic operations.

Workforce Strategy & Personnel Management: Directs overarching human resources strategy and workforce planning to adapt to changing operational demands; oversees through subordinate leadership the recruitment, selection, development, and retention of staff in accordance with UC policies and affirmative action goals.

Executive Oversight & Direct Supervision: Manages daily health system operations through the Student Health Management team, providing direct supervision and executive direction to the SHS Interim Director and the Director of Billing and Revenue Cycle.

HR Governance & Labor Relations Compliance: Maintains final departmental authority for SHS human resources decisions, working in close coordination with Student Affairs, HR, and Labor Relations to ensure strict policy adherence and contract compliance across five represented bargaining units.

Other Special Conditions Of Employment

The below licenses, certificates, credentials, bondability, altered work schedules, furloughs, travel, etc. are required for this position:

Satisfactory criminal history background check
Mandated reporting requirements of Child Abuse
Mandated reporting requirements of Dependent Adult Abuse.
Student Health requires that all clinical staff must successfully complete and pass the background check and credentialing process before employment and date of hire.
To comply with Santa Barbara County

The director of operations will encourage an engaged senior management team and guard our values. You will analyze data and metrics to evaluate staff performance, lead and encourage employees to maximize performance, and ensure a strong talent pipeline. Strong ethical leadership abilities.

Ability to make projections three years into the future.

About Third Street Community Center

The Third Street Community Center is dedicated to providing comprehensive and enriching support to Greater Downtown San Jose youth by offering educational programs that build a strong academic foundation and foster essential life skills. Through programs such as the STEM for Latina Girls and Young Engineers Program, we aim to empower low-income and underserved children to pursue a higher education and become confident, caring, and motivated individuals. Please visit our website for more information.
Summary

The Executive Director serves as the leader for the Third Street Community Center, responsible for overseeing the organization's strategic direction, operations, and programs. This role involves working closely with the Board of Directors, staff, volunteers, and community partners to fulfill the center's mission and ensure its financial sustainability.
Key Responsibilities

Leadership and Strategic Planning

Foster a positive organizational culture that promotes teamwork, innovation, diversity, and inclusivity through a social justice lens.
Collaborate with the Board of Directors to develop and implement strategic plans aligned with the organization's mission and goals.

Fund Development

Diversify our funding stream through grant writing, donation solicitation, sponsorships, donor development, and other fundraising activities.
In collaboration with the Board of Directors, assist with the annual fundraising event.

Financial Management

Develop and manage the annual operating budget in collaboration with the Board Treasurer and Bookkeeper.
Oversee financial operations including compliance with government regulations.

Human Resources

Oversee all aspects of recruiting, hiring, onboarding, and training of all employees.
Manage employees by establishing and approving work schedules, setting program expectations, and managing conflict resolution.
Oversee all aspects of volunteer recruitment, onboarding, training, and tracking of their hours on Salesforce. This includes open communication with faculty and clubs at local universities.
Serve as the Custodian of Records for all employees, contractors, and volunteers.

Community Engagement and Partnerships

Serve as the spokesperson for the agency with stakeholders, media, and the public in general.
Build and maintain relationships with our core partners, donors, elected officials, and our local community.
Serve as the administrator for all our social media channels and website, maintaining, enhancing and expanding our presence as needed.

Program Development

Ensure the effective delivery and evaluation of all agency programs by working closely with staff and volunteers.
Identify opportunities for program expansion and improvement.
Maintain high standards of program quality and participant satisfaction.

Qualifications

Bachelor's degree in education, child development, nonprofit management, business administration, or a related field; advanced degree preferred.
Demonstrated leadership experience in the nonprofit sector (or similar), with a track record of effective program management and fundraising.
Strong understanding of nonprofit budgeting, financial reporting, and resource allocation.
Excellent communication and interpersonal skills, ability to engage diverse stakeholders.
Demonstrated commitment to educational equity and social justice.
Proficiency in using technology to enhance organizational efficiency and outreach.
Spanish language proficiency is highly preferred. 

Compensation

Pay Range: $28/hr. to $32/hr., commensurate with experience and education. Benefits include health insurance, dental, professional development opportunities, and flexible work arrangements.
Application Process

Interested candidates should submit a resume and cover letter detailing their qualifications and interest in the position to info@3street.org by September 30th, 2026.

jobs.title: Executive Director
jobs.description:
Please submit your resume and cover letter to our Board President, Dana Epstein, dana@bigbigtable.org. Applicants are encouraged to apply as soon as possible.

Job Title:
Executive Director 
Location:
272 Hudson St., Buffalo, NY
Reports To:
Board Executive Committee 
Compensation:
$27/hr (approx $56,000/yr), plus Benefits (PTO, Health Insurance, & 
Employee Assistance Program available)
Type Of Position: 
Full time, 40 hrs/wk
Working Hours: 
Primarily Monday - Friday, 9am - 4pm; occasional evening meetings (usually Tuesdays), weekends and special events

About the Role

The ideal candidate is looking for a long-term position within a collaborative environment, to help lead and establish an organization in a season of stabilization and growth. As the lead staff member of a young nonprofit, this is an incredible opportunity for professional growth for a leader to help shape the future of our community café. We are seeking a highly self-motivated, adaptable, and accountable individual. Our new leader will be a solution-oriented problem-solver with a commitment to collaboration and continuous improvement. Patience, attention to detail, creativity, and the ability to hustle while remaining present with staff and volunteers are a must. 

We are seeking an energetic and people focused leader. The right person for this position will be passionate about fostering a welcome and inclusive environment, engaging a highly diverse community.

Qualifications : 

● 3+ years of leadership experience, including managing people, teams, and budgets 
● 3+ years of experience in nonprofit administration and/or hospitality management 
● 3+ years of experience in community engagement, volunteer coordination, and/or fundraising 
● Experience working with housing insecure and/or vulnerable populations 
● Dynamic and effective interpersonal skills, excellent written and verbal communication skills, strong organizational skills and attention to detail
● Ability to manage marketing and communications platforms 
● Familiarity with mental health first aid and trauma-informed practices within the community and team settings.
● Comfort with food systems and restaurant service; ability to step into the kitchen as needed 
● Spanish language proficiency, preferred 

Key Responsibilities:

Café Management 

● Maintain a welcoming, safe, and inclusive environment for guests, staff, and volunteers 
● Responsible for ensuring successful café operations, including counter service and dining area, in collaboration with the kitchen team 
● Ensure a safe and positive communal dining experience through accountability to our Community Guidelines, de-escalation support when necessary, and emergency preparedness 
● Cross-train and fill in operational gaps as needed; maintain continuity in absence of key staff 
● Collaborate with the kitchen team on resourceful, cost-effective and environmentally friendly standards and practices for sourcing of ingredients and supplies, with a strong emphasis on food rescue and sourcing locally 
● Coordinate with kitchen team to track in-kind donations 
● Oversee vendor relationships and ensure timely maintenance of facilities and equipment 

Leadership & Supervision 

● Supervise and support cafe staff and interns, including conducting performance reviews 
● Provide leadership in conflict resolution and team development 
● Guide and support internal task forces and cross-functional planning 
● Facilitate consistent internal communications, including team huddles and regularly scheduled operations meetings 
● Actively participate in and lead committee meetings as requested by the board 
● Serve as liaison between board and staff, facilitating strong communication and shared vision 
● Collaborate with staff and board on workforce development initiatives, including developing internships from local colleges and partnerships with hospitality training programs 

Fundraising & Revenue Sustainability

Build and manage a diversified funding model that may include individual giving, major gifts, corporate sponsorships, grants, fundraising events, earned revenue, and strategic partnerships.
Develop and maintain relationships with donors, foundations, corporations, community leaders and other supporters. 
Identify, research and pursue new funding opportunities aligned with Big Big Table’s mission and capacity.
Oversee the grant development process, including identifying prospects, coordinating proposals, tracking deadlines, and ensuring reporting requirements are met. 
Develop strategies to grow recurring and individual giving; create and strengthen corporate and community partnership opportunities. 
Work with cafe team to understand financial performance and identify opportunities to improve revenue, margins and operational efficiency, 
Lead and actively participate in the Fundraising Committee.

Community Engagement 

● Represent Big Big Table’s in the community through speaking engagements, coalitions, and media 
● Lead communications and outreach efforts, including social media and email platforms, to promote BBT’s mission and identity as a restaurant, attracting a diverse cross section of engagement 
● Help maintain and enhance BBT’s website and public facing platforms, including events calendar, campaigns, and promotions 
● Support volunteer engagement and onboarding systems, working with relevant staff 
● Cultivate strategic community partnerships aligned with BBT’s mission and capacity, including in-cafe resources for guests and collaborative workshops 
● Lead fundraising efforts, including donor cultivation and retention, grant writing, sponsorships, contract revenue, and events, especially the planning of our annual fundraiser Big Big Bash 
● Develop and maintain partnerships with local farmers, businesses and organizations to expand food rescue and collaborative initiatives 

Operations & Administration 

Lead and refine internal systems and operational workflows for improved efficiency 
Track and evaluate organizational data, including meals served, volunteer data, in-kind contributions, monetary donations, volunteer data, meals served, staff reports, and impact
Utilize customer relationship management tools to manage relationships with donors, volunteers, and community partners 
Support budget management and grant reporting in collaboration with the board 
Ensure appropriate documentation and information sharing across team
Ability to lift up to 50 pounds, stand for long periods of time, bend, reach, go up and down steps, work in extreme temperatures, and de-escalate guests and volunteers.
Other duties as needed

About Big Big Table Community Café 

Big Big Table Community Café (BBT) is a non-profit community café—a pay-as-you-can lunchtime restaurant, focused on addressing hunger, reducing food waste, and building community. Our motto is: “Everybody eats. Everybody gives. Everybody matters.” Our mission is to provide a dignified response to hunger in our community, providing Buffalo with accessible and affordable nutritious meals, regardless of ability to pay.
With pay-as-you-can pricing and a significant volunteer component in day-to-day operations, everyone is given a chance to earn what they need by giving what they can.

Job Summary

The Executive Director, Centralized Core Facilities provides strategic, administrative, fiscal, and operational leadership for the centralized Core Facilities at UMass Amherst within the Institute for Applied Life Sciences. A Core Facility is a multi‑user research unit that offers shared instrumentation, services, and expertise to UMass researchers, external academic partners, and industry, government, foundations or medical‑center users. The Executive Director ensures that the Core Facilities operate effectively and sustainably and that their activities align with institutional priorities and research needs.

Essential Functions

Provides strategic leadership and institutional level accountability for the centralized Core Facilities, ensuring their operational effectiveness, fiscal stability, and long-term sustainability. Directs the development and execution of the strategic plan for the Cores; in coordination with other IALS leadership, develops, implements, and oversees policies, SOPs, and MOUs related to Core Facilities; ensures completion of periodic SWOT analyses; and establishes and provides oversight of Steering Committees for centralized Core Facilities.

Directs and evaluates the work of Core Directors and Managers, establishing performance expectations, organizational priorities, workforce planning strategies and professional development objectives to ensure effective leadership across the Core Facilities.

Provides strategic financial leadership for the Core Facilities, interpreting financial information to guide operational decisions and long-range planning in conjunction with the Finance & Operations Director, IALS. Serves as a principal advisor to the Director, IALS, and the IALS Executive committee on the long-term plan for each core, including capital and operational investment, transference, and operational risk of the core.

Provides strategic oversight of equipment planning and lifecycle management across the Core Facilities. Identifies and prioritizes equipment needs (new acquisitions and updates); develops repair and replacement timetables with projected budget estimates and justifications; monitors equipment usage and duty cycle percentages for each Core to inform planning and prioritization; and provides guidance on equipment related components of faculty start up packages and equipment match proposals, ensuring incoming faculty are aware of Core Facilities capabilities.

Provides leadership and coordination for grant application activities across the Core Facilities. Prioritizes applications by need and institutional impact; develops and maintains a grant submissions calendar; prepares justification and information slide decks outlining space, staffing, cost, and revenue implications; and contributes to application teams (typically including a Core Director and key PIs).

Provides strategic oversight and analysis of Core Facilities performance, utilizing financial reports prepared by the Director of Finance & Operations, who manages all operational financial management. Defines and standardizes portfolio-wide financial and impact metrics; implements dashboards and scorecards to monitor performance; and uses aggregated data to inform strategic decisions regarding portfolio composition, pricing, investment, marketing, and service sunsetting. Prepares synthesized Core Facilities performance reports for senior leadership and advisory committees.

Provides oversight of space and infrastructure planning across the Core Facilities. Provides guidance on the prioritization and need for service contracts across the Core Facilities. Provides oversight of training expectations and compliance across the Core Facilities. jobs.title: Development Director
jobs.description:
NC Local is looking for an experienced fundraiser and development strategist to lead and grow our philanthropic efforts, with an emphasis on major donors.
Location:
NC-based, remote position, with preference for candidates in the Charlotte or Triangle areas
Reports to:
CEO
Salary:
Starting at $115,000

About NC Local

NC Local is a statewide nonprofit newsroom on a mission to connect North Carolinians to the issues shaping their lives. We make complex state issues understandable and useful, hold public institutions accountable, and help communities become more informed and civically engaged.

We started our journey by asking people across North Carolina what news and information they needed most. Since launching in fall 2025, we've surfaced stories no one else was covering, brought communities together around critical issues at events, and built partnerships with newsrooms and other organizations across the state. We've also secured investments from major philanthropic institutions and a growing base of donors who see NC Local's vision and path to scale.

Now we're growing our team to reach our next level of impact. This role will shape the strategy that carries NC Local from its launch year to a sustainable organization that serves every part of this state. It's an opportunity to join a well-backed startup and help a dedicated team shape it into an enduring statewide institution.

Position Overview

NC Local is looking for an experienced fundraiser and development strategist to lead and grow our philanthropic efforts, with an emphasis on major donors.

This leadership role is a newly-created position for NC Local, an early-stage nonprofit newsroom that’s on an ambitious growth path with major investments from the Knight Foundation and the American Journalism Project. As Development Director, you’ll own our fundraising strategy and build and develop a portfolio of major donors, working closely with the CEO to develop an individual donor program and cultivate our current and prospective institutional funders.

You’ll also build and direct our development team, including overseeing two future team members—a development manager and associate—and working closely with our membership manager on individual giving strategies. This is a cross-functional role that will collaborate with colleagues across editorial teams, operations and executive leadership, and with NC Local’s board, which is engaged in our growth strategy.

We seek a candidate who is creative, strategic and entrepreneurial. Exceptional relationship-building and communication skills are critical, as this position requires an ability to translate vision into investment and present why local journalism matters in a persuasive, compelling way to a variety of stakeholders. The ideal candidate is also a goal-oriented self-starter whose work can be organized and executed independently. We also seek a candidate who brings the adaptability and resourcefulness needed to operate successfully in an early stage organization, where moving comfortably between advancing our strategic direction, developing organizational systems and performing a variety of tasks can be adeptly balanced.

The ideal candidate will have a successful and demonstrated track record in these areas and operate in ways grounded in NC Local’s mission and values. While it is not a requirement to have a background in journalism or the media industry, it is important to carry a passion and appreciation for the importance of factual, accessible and useful news and information. This role offers an opportunity to help a growing organization reach its next level of impact and help build more informed and civically engaged communities across North Carolina.

This is a remote, North Carolina-based position, with preference for candidates based in the greater Charlotte and Triangle areas. Travel across the state and to industry convenings and team meetings is expected. 

What you'll do

Major gifts and individual giving

Build our major gifts program from the ground up and develop it as one of the primary sources of revenue for NC Local’s future.
Develop and carry a portfolio of major donors and prospects who give more than $5,000 annually, meeting regularly for conversations about local news and information needs and making direct, in-person asks for support.
Create and direct campaigns that drive transformational gifts for NC Local’s major initiatives.
Build the prospect pipeline from research through cultivation to close.
Work with the membership manager to connect small-dollar giving to the major gifts pipeline, so members with capacity expand their support.
Design the stewardship that keeps donors giving — reporting, recognition and the touch points that aren't direct asks.

Team development and board coordination

Hire, onboard and develop the development team and supervise their progress toward our fundraising strategy.
Develop systems and processes for the development team.
Supervise staff while fostering collaboration, growth and accountability.
Partner with CEO and Board to grow giving and turn board relationships into prospects.
Present strategic updates to the Board, coordinating their role in fundraising and developments.

Strategy and planning

Help devise and lead a comprehensive, donor-centered fundraising program with specific goals that will create the foundation of support for NC Local’s important and ambitious growth.
Oversee existing fundraising strategy and revise for new targets and developments.
Work closely with the CEO to develop and execute multi-year plans around outreach, relationship building, and pitching to align with annual budget needs and growth strategy.
Develop strategies for funding program development, working closely with colleagues across the organization, funders and other partners.
Keep our case for support current as the organization evolves.
Help prepare concept notes, proposals, grant reports and donor-facing materials.
Support the development of an annual report, communicating the impact of philanthropically supported work.

Movement-building and relationship development

Plan meetings, events and other convenings to draw awareness about NC Local’s impact and vision, and bring prospective donors together with our team.
Prospect, cultivate and nurture institutional funding relationships to secure major gifts and foundation grants.
Serve as a leading voice about the need for philanthropic funding for local news and the importance of local news for North Carolina communities.

Commitment to diversity and inclusivity

NC Local is building an inclusive team that represents the diversity and multifaceted nature of our state across geography, demographics, culture and other lived experiences. We welcome talented individuals from all backgrounds who bring curiosity, dedication and a drive to succeed. If you’re interested in this role but don’t meet every listed criteria, we encourage you to apply anyway. We are looking for people who want to grow, contribute and make an impact.

What you'll bring to the organization

You're an experienced fundraiser with at least 6 years of increasing responsibility in nonprofit development, and you've closed individual gifts in the five and six figures.
You've raised money from both individuals and foundations, and you can point to relationships you built rather than inherited. You understand the complexity of donor relationships, and you are unafraid of the ask.
You write well and quickly — proposals, donor letters, briefing memos, and the note that has to go out before tomorrow's meeting.
You've managed people and have developed the skills to lead
You use data and other evidence to set fundraising goals and the strategies to achieve them. 
You are experienced with CRMs, prospect research and portfolio management.
You can explain why local journalism matters to someone who has never thought about it and leave them wanting to help.
You work independently in a fast-paced, entrepreneurial environment and can work hands-on, not just direct a strategy.
You're comfortable working in an early-stage organization that’s still developing processes and policies, and you’re willing to help.
You have excellent communication skills, including the ability to write compelling donor communications and fundraising pitches.

You’ll stand out if:

You have raised money for nonprofit organizations in North Carolina and can bring relationships with you.
You’ve built a development function at an early-stage organization and managed a fundraising team.
You can talk clearly and effectively about the importance of journalism and NC Local’s mission, even if you’ve never worked in journalism

Compensation & benefits
NC Local is a remote organization and candidates must live in or relocate to North Carolina.
This is a salaried, full-time position. The starting salary for this position is $115,000, with the possibility of a higher level for the most experienced and qualified candidates. This position is funded with support from the American Journalism Project. Employees can participate in an employer-sponsored health insurance plan, including vision and dental coverage; paid time off and holidays in accordance with NC Local policy; and a 401(k) plan.

Submit a detailed resume and cover letter via this link: bit.ly/nclocal_development

tl;dr
Co-lead Permit Power’s policy development to simplify and streamline permitting, inspection, HOAs, building codes, and product standards to dramatically lower the cost and accelerate the adoption of residential rooftop solar, plug-in solar, and home batteries.

What we do at Permit Power 

Permit Power is an energy affordability non-profit on a mission to make it cheap and easy for American families to power their lives by cutting the red tape that makes home solar and batteries so expensive. 

We are a small but ambitious team that advances common-sense policy fixes in states around the country to modernize processes like permitting and utility interconnection to allow tens of millions more American families to produce their own affordable electricity. 

What you’ll be doing: 

We are looking for a Permitting Policy Director to co-lead our agenda to remove bureaucratic barriers for residential rooftop solar, plug-in solar, and home batteries, including streamlining permitting, inspection, homeowner association approvals, and codes and standards. In partnership with Permit Power’s advocacy staff, you’ll serve as a core part of our team to drive legislative change, lead and participate in coalition efforts, and be an internal expert and external thought leader on permit streamlining. A significant portion of your work will likely focus on policies derived from the values of property rights, small government, and consumer choice in conservative and purple states. The specific policies and states will be divided with Permit Power’s current Permitting Policy Director based on existing expertise, geography, and other factors. You will report to the Chief of Policy.
Develop Permit Power's permitting policy agenda:
Formulate and execute a comprehensive policy plan to simplify and streamline permitting and inspection processes for home solar and batteries, with a focus on states with the largest home solar and battery potential, as well as simplifying and streamlining building codes and product safety standards for home solar products such as plug-in solar.  
Oversee the bill-to-law cycle:
Conduct preliminary research for, draft, and vet permitting bill language. Produce advocacy materials, such as talking points, fact sheets, graphics, and reports. In coordination with Permit Power’s advocacy team and outside lobbyists, lobby legislators, their staff, and executive branch officials. Negotiate with opposition. 
Build and drive coalitions:
Develop and manage relationships with partners such as home builders, the solar industry, think tanks, and others to broaden support for a permitting reform agenda and to collaboratively refine and update our state policy priorities.  
Serve as the subject matter expert:
Act as the organization's authority on permitting rules, regulations, and cutting-edge policies like third party permitting and inspection, HOA overreach, and simplified building codes and product standards.
Evaluate compliance and implementation:
Investigate whether jurisdictions are following the bills we pass, whether installers are actively taking advantage of them, and why. Then analyze where implementation is hitting friction points and refine solutions to remove further and persistent barriers to affordable home solar and batteries.
Manage external research and consultants:
Scope external policy research and identify, onboard, and direct consultants to secure high-quality products supporting our permitting policy agenda.

What we’re looking for:  

7+ years of experience in policy development, legislative advocacy, and/or regulatory affairs related to solar, construction, permitting, or government efficiency.
Track record of successfully developing and executing policy agendas that lead to tangible outcomes, particularly within the state legislative arenas.
Sufficient technical expertise with relevant engineering concepts (e.g., electrical, structural, and/or fire safety) to shape our policy approach to permitting and inspection policies, building codes, and product safety standards.
Experience testifying before, interfacing with, and developing materials for policymakers.
Demonstrated ability to build coalitions and partner with stakeholders to achieve policy goals.
Ability to translate complex technical and engineering concepts into clear, accessible language and materials for policymakers, advocates, and the public.
Relationships with energy policy organizations, the building industry, technical consultants, research firms, and think tanks.

What will make you a good fit: 

Entrepreneurial and self-directed.
We are a small team, and you will need to be able to figure out what your goals are and how to achieve them within the set timeframe. 
Outcomes-oriented.
We measure ourselves by how much we can drive down the cost and timelines for installing solar and batteries, and how much more solar and batteries are installed as a result of our work. We are looking for someone who will find fulfillment in achieving those concrete goals. 
Collaborative and low-ego
. We’re a start-up organization and will make many mistakes. We will only succeed if we work together, acknowledge our mistakes, and learn from them. 
Flexible and open-minded.

Comfortable collaborating and finding common ground with stakeholders across the ideological spectrum
Organized and detail-oriented.
No one will be looking over your shoulder, and you will need to take true ownership over the quality of your work and stay on top of your own administrative work. 
Occasional travel:
Willing to travel for team meetings and periodic partner meetings, hearings, and conferences several times a year.

In partnership with Permit Power’s advocacy staff, you’ll serve as a core part of our team to drive legislative change, lead and participate in coalition efforts, and be an internal expert and external thought leader on permit streamlining. A significant portion of your work will likely focus on policies derived from the values of property rights, small government, and consumer choice in conservative and purple states. The specific policies and states will be divided with Permit Power’s current Permitting Policy Director based on existing expertise, geography, and other factors. You will report to the Chief of Policy.
Develop Permit Power's permitting policy agenda:
Formulate and execute a comprehensive policy plan to simplify and streamline permitting and inspection processes for home solar and batteries, with a focus on states with the largest home solar and battery potential, as well as simplifying and streamlining building codes and product safety standards for home solar products such as plug-in solar.  
Oversee the bill-to-law cycle:
Conduct preliminary research for, draft, and vet permitting bill language. Produce advocacy materials, such as talking points, fact sheets, graphics, and reports. In coordination with Permit Power’s advocacy team and outside lobbyists, lobby legislators, their staff, and executive branch officials. Negotiate with opposition. 
Build and drive coalitions:
Develop and manage relationships with partners such as home builders, the solar industry, think tanks, and others to broaden support for a permitting reform agenda and to collaboratively refine and update our state policy priorities.  
Serve as the subject matter expert:
Act as the organization's authority on permitting rules, regulations, and cutting-edge policies like third party permitting and inspection, HOA overreach, and simplified building codes and product standards.
Evaluate compliance and implementation:
Investigate whether jurisdictions are following the bills we pass, whether installers are actively taking advantage of them, and why. Then analyze where implementation is hitting friction points and refine solutions to remove further and persistent barriers to affordable home solar and batteries.
Manage external research and consultants:
Scope external policy research and identify, onboard, and direct consultants to secure high-quality products supporting our permitting policy agenda.

What we’re looking for:  

7+ years of experience in policy development, legislative advocacy, and/or regulatory affairs related to solar, construction, permitting, or government efficiency.
Track record of successfully developing and executing policy agendas that lead to tangible outcomes, particularly within the state legislative arenas.
Sufficient technical expertise with relevant engineering concepts (e.g., electrical, structural, and/or fire safety) to shape our policy approach to permitting and inspection policies, building codes, and product safety standards.
Experience testifying before, interfacing with, and developing materials for policymakers.
Demonstrated ability to build coalitions and partner with stakeholders to achieve policy goals.
Ability to translate complex technical and engineering concepts into clear, accessible language and materials for policymakers, advocates, and the public.
Relationships with energy policy organizations, the building industry, technical consultants, research firms, and think tanks.

What will make you a good fit: 

Entrepreneurial and self-directed.
We are a small team, and you will need to be able to figure out what your goals are and how to achieve them within the set timeframe. 
Outcomes-oriented.
We measure ourselves by how much we can drive down the cost and timelines for installing solar and batteries, and how much more solar and batteries are installed as a result of our work. We are looking for someone who will find fulfillment in achieving those concrete goals. 
Collaborative and low-ego
. We’re a start-up organization and will make many mistakes. We will only succeed if we work together, acknowledge our mistakes, and learn from them. 
Flexible and open-minded.

Comfortable collaborating and finding common ground with stakeholders across the ideological spectrum
Organized and detail-oriented.
No one will be looking over your shoulder, and you will need to take true ownership over the quality of your work and stay on top of your own administrative work. 
Occasional travel:
Willing to travel for team meetings and periodic partner meetings, hearings, and conferences several times a year. 

The salary & benefits you can expect: 

The salary range for this position is $135,000-160,000. This is a full-time, exempt position. Permit Power offers a generous and comprehensive benefits package including health insurance, dental insurance, vision care, pre-tax commuter benefits, FSA, 401k with 5% contribution matching (limits apply). 
Permit Power offers 6 months of paid maternity or paternity leave to bond with a newborn or adopted child within the first year of birth or adoption. 
We are a fully remote team open to candidates anywhere in the U.S.

new_jobs.description:
Director of Advancement
Organization:
EMBRACE - Enriching Many By Reaching All In Catholic Education
Reports to:
Executive Director
Employment:
Full-Time
Location:
Kansas City metropolitan area preferred; regular travel throughout the Archdiocese of Kansas City in Kansas required
About EMBRACE
EMBRACE is a 501(c)(3) nonprofit organization committed to providing opportunities for inclusive education by supporting students with disabilities and learning differences in Catholic schools. Since 2018, EMBRACE has invested millions of dollars in grants and scholarships supporting students, teachers, and Catholic schools across the Archdiocese of Kansas City in Kansas.
As EMBRACE continues to grow, we are seeking a Director of Advancement to help build the organization's fundraising capacity, expand our donor base, strengthen relationships with current and prospective supporters, and create new opportunities to increase our impact.
Position Summary
The Director of Advancement will lead EMBRACE's fundraising and development efforts and work closely with the Executive Director to grow revenue, expand the donor base, strengthen donor relationships, and build a sustainable development program.
This is a relationship-driven, results-oriented position requiring someone who is comfortable developing relationships, making fundraising asks, writing grants, pursuing corporate and foundation support, and identifying new opportunities for EMBRACE.
The ideal candidate will bring strong fundraising skills and a genuine passion for ensuring that every student, regardless of ability, has the opportunity to learn, belong, and thrive in a Catholic school.
This person should be inspired by EMBRACE's mission and motivated by the opportunity to help Catholic schools become more inclusive and supportive of all students and families.

Key Responsibilities
Fundraising Strategy
Develop and implement an annual development plan and fundraising strategy in partnership with the Executive Director.
Establish fundraising goals, track progress, and measure results through defined KPIs.
Identify new opportunities to diversify and grow EMBRACE's revenue.
Build a sustainable fundraising program that supports EMBRACE's long-term growth and mission.

Major Gifts & Individual Giving
Identify, cultivate, solicit, and steward major gift prospects and donors.
Build and manage a strong major gift pipeline and develop strategies to increase individual giving.
Conduct donor visits and develop meaningful, long-term relationships with individuals and families.
Identify opportunities to acquire, retain, and upgrade donors through thoughtful cultivation and stewardship.

Grants & Foundation Relations
Grant development will be a significant and ongoing responsibility of this position.
Research and identify foundation, corporate, and other grant opportunities aligned with EMBRACE's mission and programs.
Write and submit compelling grant proposals, letters of inquiry, and other funding requests.
Manage grant deadlines, reporting requirements, renewals, and ongoing communication with funders.
Work with the Executive Director to identify funding needs and develop strategies to maximize grant revenue.

Corporate & Foundation Partnerships
Identify and cultivate corporate and foundation prospects and develop long-term funding relationships.
Develop sponsorship opportunities and strategies to increase corporate support.
Build partnerships with businesses and organizations that align with EMBRACE's mission.
Work with the Executive Director to cultivate, solicit, and steward corporate and foundation partners.

Donor Stewardship
Develop and implement strategies to retain and deepen relationships with EMBRACE donors.
Ensure donors understand the impact of their support and the difference EMBRACE makes in Catholic schools.
Maintain accurate donor and prospect records and track cultivation, solicitation, and stewardship activities.
Create meaningful opportunities for donors to remain engaged with EMBRACE and its mission.

Events
Support EMBRACE fundraising events with a focus on maximizing revenue and donor engagement.
Develop and manage event sponsorship opportunities.
Use events to identify, cultivate, and engage prospective donors and corporate partners.
Follow up with attendees, sponsors, and prospects to develop long-term relationships beyond the event.

Community & Relationship Development
Represent EMBRACE throughout the Kansas City metropolitan area and the broader Archdiocese of Kansas City in Kansas.
Build relationships with parish leaders, Catholic school leaders, business leaders, community organizations, donors, and prospective supporters.
Regularly meet with donors, prospects, corporate partners, foundation representatives, and other stakeholders.
Identify opportunities to increase EMBRACE's visibility, community relationships, and philanthropic support.

Measures of Success
Success will be measured by both fundraising results and the development of a sustainable fundraising program, including:
Growth in philanthropic revenue, including individual, corporate, foundation, grant, and sponsorship support.
Growth in the number of donors, donor retention, average gift size, and major gift pipeline.
Successful pursuit, submission, and management of grant opportunities and funding relationships.
Development of systems, relationships, and strategies that position EMBRACE for continued long-term growth.

Specific annual fundraising goals and KPIs will be established with the Executive Director.
Qualifications
5+ years of professional fundraising/development experience preferred.
Demonstrated success in major gifts, individual giving, grant writing, or corporate/foundation relations.
Strong grant-writing, communication, relationship-building, and organizational skills.
Experience developing and managing a fundraising pipeline and comfortable cultivating and soliciting donors.
Ability to work independently, manage multiple priorities, and meet deadlines.
Knowledge of the Kansas City philanthropic community strongly preferred.
Experience working with Catholic organizations or Catholic education preferred but not required.
Commitment to EMBRACE's mission and Catholic education.
Ability and willingness to travel throughout the Archdiocese of Kansas City in Kansas.
Valid driver's license and reliable transportation.

Ideal Candidate
The ideal candidate is passionate about EMBRACE's mission and believes strongly that every student, regardless of ability, should have the opportunity to receive an inclusive Catholic education.
They are a strategic, entrepreneurial, and relationship-oriented fundraiser who is comfortable working independently, building meaningful relationships, making asks, writing grants, pursuing new funding opportunities, and delivering measurable results.
The successful candidate will be someone who sees the potential for EMBRACE to grow significantly and is excited about helping build the infrastructure, relationships, and revenue necessary to expand the organization's impact.
This person should bring energy, creativity, persistence, and a strong sense of ownership to the role and be equally comfortable meeting with a major donor, writing a grant proposal, developing a corporate partnership, following up with an event sponsor, or traveling across the Archdiocese to build a new relationship.
Compensation
EMBRACE will establish a competitive compensation package based on the scope of the position, experience, organizational resources, and mutually agreed-upon performance expectations.
The compensation structure may include a base salary and performance-based compensation tied to established fundraising goals and KPIs.

Secure major gifts of $25,000 or more from qualified donors and prospects.

Expand the qualified major donor pipeline throughout the Midwest region.

Identify and refer appropriate planned giving opportunities.

Develop strong partnerships with affiliates and Foundation leadership to advance fundraising opportunities.

Maintain accurate and timely donor and moves management information within Salesforce.

Bachelor’s degree required.

Experience managing a strategic major gift portfolio utilizing moves management best practices.

Experience utilizing Salesforce or a comparable CRM platform.

Proven ability to develop trusted relationships with high-net-worth individuals and families.

Strong consultative fundraising, donor cultivation, solicitation, and stewardship skills.

Excellent written, verbal, interpersonal, and presentation skills.

Strong organizational, project management, and time management abilities.

Ability to work independently while collaborating effectively across a geographically dispersed organization.

Demonstrated initiative, sound judgment, accountability, and discretion.

Knowledge of planned giving principles preferred.

Supervisory Responsibilities
This position has no supervisory responsibilities.

Work Environment & Travel
This is a full-time, remote position supporting the Midwest region.

Approximately 50% travel
is required throughout the assigned territory for donor visits, affiliate engagement, conferences, Foundation meetings, national events, and other fundraising activities.
